rule.definition: Warn on retaining an earlier interface around its replacement contrary to the applicable clean-break policy. Require complete evidence of retention and whether an independent boundary requires this retained interface. Useful behavior alone does not justify retaining it; an independent requirement can arise in the same change. Unknown evidence is not compliance, and a warning does not establish that deletion is safe.

criteria.true: Complete relevant before/after definitions and known surface/exception context establish whether an earlier interface is retained. For a retained wrapper, its complete definition, replacement contract and enough context to determine whether an independent boundary requires retaining that interface are supplied. No independent responsibility need exist. A complete clean break or independently added wrapper can establish no retention.
criteria.false: At least one required definition, interface history, policy fact or boundary fact is missing or ambiguous.

criteria.true: The change retains an earlier callable, name, argument or return interface through its replacement. This includes pure forwarding, aliases and adaptation done to retain that earlier interface.
criteria.false: The supplied evidence establishes no retention of a replaced interface. Forwarding by itself or missing history does not establish compatibility retention.

criteria.true: Supplied contract, registration, caller or test evidence establishes an independent requirement for this retained interface and its protocol, validation, instrumentation or other responsibility. The requirement may arise in the same change. Useful behavior or a new test alone does not justify keeping an old interface when the replacement could own that behavior without losing the boundary.
criteria.false: The covered evidence establishes either no retained wrapper or compatibility-only retention with no independent requirement for the retained interface. Adding gratuitous validation or instrumentation does not create such a requirement. Missing purpose evidence cannot establish this outcome.
